The dangerous thing about being in an industry for too long is that you fail to understand bottom-up developments, e.g. Bitcoin maximalist canceling altcoins, and $ETH. It's important to keep an open mind (still not buying $DOGE though, probably because of my 2017 PTSD) #crypto

I'm not implying that $DOGE will flip $BTC. But unlike many critics say, $DOGE frankly has a purpose; providing the first interactions with blockchain technology for a relatively large audience, just like Atari consoles provided the first interaction with computing technology.

History doesn't always repeat, but it often rhymes. Relate Atari to $DOGE, and the amusing Shiba Inu memecoin suddenly compares as a major kickstarter for human-crypto interaction. In short, games and memes made, and are making new technology understandable for the average Joe.

The destiny of $DOGE (thread✌). In the 1970s, Atari gaming machines were so successful that they frequently broke down because of al the cash inside them. Once, Atari was the most profitable computer business in the world. Games really kick-started the human-computer dialogue.
